question: Who assumed the Chairmanship of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in May 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is **Ajay Kumar.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
**Dr. Ajay Kumar, **Former Secretary, Ministry of Defence took the Oath of Office and Secrecy as Chairman, Union Public Service Commission today.

 
 
• 
 
The Oath was administered by Lt.Gen. Raj Shukla (Retd.), the senior most Member of the Commission.

 
 
• 
 
Having pursued a B.Tech. in Electrical Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur, Dr. Ajay Kumar has done his M.S. in Applied Economics from the University of Minnesota, USA and Ph.D in Business Administration from Carlson School of Management, University of Minnesota, USA. He was also conferred an Hon. Doctor of Philosophy by Amity University in 2019.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC):**

 
 
• The UPSC is a **constitutional body** established under **Article 315 of the Constitution of India**.
 
• It is responsible for conducting examinations and selecting candidates for various civil services and posts in the Government of India.
 
• The commission also advises the President of India on matters related to recruitment, promotions, and disciplinary cases.
 
• It conducts prominent examinations like the Civil Services Examination, Indian Forest Service Examination, Engineering Services Examination, and others.
 
 
 
• **Role of the UPSC Chairman:**
 
 
• The Chairman leads the commission, ensuring fair and transparent processes in recruitment.
 
• The position requires integrity, impartiality, and administrative acumen to oversee operations and uphold the commission's reputation.
 
• The chairman is appointed by the President of India and generally serves until the age of 65 or completion of tenure.
 
 
 
• **Importance of UPSC in Governance:**
 
 
• The UPSC ensures merit-based recruitment for India's civil services, essential for effective governance and administration.
 
• It plays a crucial role in shaping the bureaucracy that implements policies and drives development.
 
• The commission’s independence and impartiality uphold the principles of democracy and good governance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Age and Tenure of UPSC Chairman:**

 
 
• The Chairman of UPSC usually serves until the age of **65 years** or completion of their tenure.
 
• The tenure is designed to ensure continuity and stability in the commission’s functioning.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• The UPSC operates under the framework of **Articles 315 to 323** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The provisions ensure independence and autonomy, critical for unbiased decision-making in recruitment processes.
